mcp.instructions: MQTT Panel is a desktop MQTT client with a built-in broker. These tools act in the running app; the user sees every change in its window. Writing tools work once the user has accepted the acknowledgement in MQTT Panel (Settings, Assistant). For passwords, keys and passphrases use ask_in_app true: MQTT Panel asks the user itself and the secret never passes through the chat. Ask the user before deleting anything or skipping certificate verification.
mcp.prompt.connect.title: Connect me to a broker
mcp.prompt.connect.description: Create or fix a connection, handle TLS and certificates, test, and connect.
mcp.prompt.connect.address: The broker address, if already known (host, port, protocol).
mcp.prompt.connect.body:
Help me connect MQTT Panel to an MQTT broker. Use the app's tools step by step:
1. Call list_connections to see what exists; reuse a connection that matches.
2. Unless I already said so, ask me for the broker address (host and port) and whether it uses TLS (mqtts, wss) or WebSocket. Then call create_connection or update_connection.
3. If the broker needs a login, ask for the username and set it with update_connection. For the password call set_connection_password with ask_in_app true, so I type it in MQTT Panel and it never passes through this chat.
4. For a private CA call set_ca_certificate with ask_in_app true. If the broker wants a client certificate, ask whether I have one (set_client_certificate with ask_in_app true) or need a new key (generate_client_key, get_client_csr, then import_signed_certificate once it is signed).
5. Call test_connection. If it reports a certificate MQTT Panel cannot verify, show me its details and ask which trust choice I want, then call trust_certificate with it. Never choose skip_once or skip_always on your own.
6. When the test succeeds, call connect, then show_connection. Explain any error in plain words and propose the fix.
mcp.prompt.why.title: Why can't I connect?
mcp.prompt.why.description: Read the last error and the certificate question of a connection and propose the fix.
mcp.prompt.why.connection: The connection to look at (name or id); all of them when omitted.
mcp.prompt.why.state: Current state of the connections (no secrets):
mcp.prompt.why.body:
A connection in MQTT Panel does not work. Find out why and propose the fix:
1. Read the state below (last error and last test of each connection). If that is not enough, call test_connection for the connection.
2. Explain the error in plain words: wrong host or port, nothing listening, TLS on a plain port or the reverse, login refused, client certificate missing, certificate not trusted.
3. Propose one concrete fix and, once I agree, apply it with update_connection, set_connection_password (ask_in_app true), set_ca_certificate (ask_in_app true) or trust_certificate (ask me which choice; never skip verification on your own).
4. Test again, then connect.
